problems.title: Staffing strategy
problems.question: How should the restaurant staff its weekdays and weekends?

options.name: Keep current staffing
cons: Idle-labour cost continues on quiet days
Weekend overload (if any) continues

modifiers.reason: Staffing mismatch is supported, so keeping things as they are continues the cost.
Weekend overload or reliability problems are supported and would continue.
There is no evidence of staffing waste, so change is less urgent.

options.name: Demand-based scheduling with daily-wage staff
options.summary: Fewer staff on quiet weekdays, extra daily-wage workers on busy days.
pros: Uses flexible daily-wage workers (common in Pakistani restaurants)
Can fix weekday waste and weekend shortage together
cons: Needs a weekly roster and a reliable pool of daily workers
Regular staff may resist changed shifts

modifiers.reason: Labour not matched to demand is supported, and this option addresses it directly.
Weekend demand is at least twice weekday demand, so flexible staffing has large room to help.
Adds cover on the busy days where capacity is a problem.
No evidence of staffing waste, so rescheduling gains little.

options.name: Add weekend daily-wage workers only
options.summary: Keep weekday staffing, hire extra people for peak days.
pros: Simple to explain and to start
cons: Adds payroll without cutting weekday idle time
Benefit depends on weekend sales really being lost today

modifiers.reason: Weekend capacity problems are supported, and this adds cover exactly there.
Extra payroll while weekday idle time exists adds to cost.
No evidence of weekend capacity problems, so extra workers may not pay for themselves.

options.name: Reduce the permanent workforce
options.summary: Cut a share of permanent staff to lower fixed labour cost.
pros: Quick effect on the profit line
cons: Service quality and morale may fall
Redundancy is hard to reverse and can hurt weekends

modifiers.reason: Staffing mismatch is strongly supported.
Service is already stretched, so cutting staff is risky.
Labour cost is above 45% of sales, so the saving is large.

problems.title: Cost and margin improvement
problems.question: Which action should be tried first to improve profit margins?

options.name: Do nothing for now
cons: Margin pressure continues

modifiers.reason: Wastage is supported and would continue.
Rising food cost is supported and would continue.

options.name: Prepare food by weekday/weekend demand
options.summary: Forecast daily demand and cook accordingly.
cons: Needs daily sales records and discipline
Risk of running out if forecast is too tight

modifiers.reason: Food wastage is supported and this option targets it.
You prepare the same quantity every day despite uneven demand.
No evidence of food wastage.

options.name: Renegotiate suppliers and tighten purchasing
options.summary: Compare quotes, consolidate orders, check portion sizes.
cons: Cheaper suppliers may reduce quality
Takes owner time to negotiate

modifiers.reason: Rising food cost is supported.
Weak inventory control is supported; tighter purchasing helps.
No evidence of rising food cost.

options.name: Menu re-engineering
options.summary: Promote high-margin dishes, redesign or drop low-margin ones.
pros: Improves profit per plate without losing customers
cons: Needs dish costing
Customers may dislike menu changes

modifiers.reason: A low-margin menu mix is supported.
Pricing weakness is supported; menu design helps.
No evidence of a low-margin menu mix.

options.name: Reform the discount policy
options.summary: Limit discounts to quiet hours and measure results.
cons: Customers used to offers may leave
Needs careful testing

modifiers.reason: Discount-driven margin erosion is supported.
Sales depend on discounts, so cutting them is risky.
No evidence of discount-driven margin loss.

problems.title: Cash-flow recovery
problems.question: What should be done first to relieve cash pressure?

options.name: Do nothing for now
cons: Cash pressure may worsen

modifiers.reason: Cash pressure is supported and may get worse.

options.name: Collect receivables and enforce payment terms
options.summary: Follow up overdue amounts and set clear credit terms.
pros: Releases cash that is already yours
cons: Pressure on corporate clients may affect relationships
Only works if receivables are real

modifiers.reason: Overdue receivables are high, so collection has large potential.
A working-capital imbalance is supported.
Overdue receivables are small, so there is little to collect.

options.name: Negotiate longer supplier terms or reschedule payables
options.summary: Ask suppliers for extra credit days.
pros: Quick relief with no interest if agreed
cons: Suppliers may raise prices or limit supply
Hides rather than fixes the problem

modifiers.reason: Cash pressure is supported, so extra time helps.
Already relying on supplier credit; more reliance is risky.

options.name: Restructure or reschedule loan instalments
options.summary: Talk to the lender about lower or later instalments.
cons: May increase total interest paid
Approval is not guaranteed

modifiers.reason: Debt burden is supported.
Instalments take a large share of sales.
No evidence of a debt problem.

options.name: Cut non-essential costs
options.summary: Trim utilities, extras and low-value spending.
pros: Immediate and fully in your control
cons: Limited size of saving
Cutting the wrong item can hurt service

modifiers.reason: A heavy fixed-cost burden is supported.
Cash pressure is supported; every saving counts.

problems.title: Branch / franchise decision
problems.question: What should be done with the weakest branch?

options.name: Keep all branches open as they are
cons: Losses (if any) continue
Branches may compete for the same customers

modifiers.reason: The weakest branch is losing money.
Branches follow almost the same trend, which suggests they compete for the same customers.
The weakest branch is improving month by month.

options.name: Close the weakest branch and focus on the others
options.summary: Shut the weakest branch, move staff and effort to stronger branches.
pros: Stops losses at the weak branch
cons: Some customers will be lost
Closing is hard to reverse

modifiers.reason: The weakest branch loses money, so closing removes the loss.
Customers can move to the sibling branch because both serve the same market.
The branch is improving, so closing may be premature.

options.name: Invest in and promote the weakest branch
options.summary: Marketing, menu refresh or renovation to lift sales.
pros: Keeps the brand present in that area
cons: Needs cash, which may be limited
Results are uncertain

modifiers.reason: The trend is flat or improving, so investment has a base to build on.
A sibling branch already serves the same customers.
Deep losses make investment risky.

options.name: Convert the weakest branch to delivery-only
options.summary: Cut dining costs and serve online orders from a smaller kitchen.
cons: Loses dine-in customers
Needs delivery platform and packaging

modifiers.reason: Lower running cost suits a loss-making branch.
Delivery orders are already declining.
